instruction: The stack exports `SshCommand` as `{{reference-architectures-EC2-instance-us-east-1-SshCommand}}` which looks like I should be able to ssh directly to the public DNS. From my laptop on the public internet it times out, but a colleague on the corporate VPN says the command works for them. Trace what access is actually possible end to end against instance {{reference-architectures-EC2-instance-us-east-1-InstanceId}}.
expected_answer: The `SshCommand` export is misleading: external SSH does not work even though the instance has a public IP, because the SSH security group restricts port 22 to the VPC CIDR (10.0.0.0/16), not 0.0.0.0/0. The deployed topology: the instance has two security groups attached. The Ec2InstanceSG has no ingress rules at all. The Ec2SshSecurityGroup has a single ingress rule allowing all traffic from 10.0.0.0/16 (the VPC CIDR). The instance sits in a public subnet with a public IP, but packets arriving at port 22 from any non-VPC source are dropped by the security group. Your colleague's VPN may route them through the VPC CIDR range, or they may be using SSM Session Manager (which does not require inbound ingress). What actually works is SSM Session Manager: the instance IAM role has AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore attached, and `aws ssm start-session --target {{reference-architectures-EC2-instance-us-east-1-InstanceId}}` reaches the instance without needing any security group ingress rule. Net: use SSM Session Manager, not direct SSH.
